# NEUTROPENIC FEVER

## Inpatient/Outpatient/ER

The risk of severe, rapidly progressive infections increases when the absolute neutrophil count (ANC, segmented neutrophils plus bands) is less than 500 cells/microliter. The risk increases dramatically when the ANC is <100 cells/microliter. Because of these risks, patients with fever and neutropenia to this degree should receive empirical antimicrobial therapy immediately. Empirical therapy should also be given to patients with fever and ANC 500-1000 cells/microliter when the concentration is expected to be <500 cells/microliter within the next 48 hours. For this purpose, fever is defined as a single temperature greater than 38.3 degrees Celsius.

Therapy:
## Initial therapy

Since infection can be rapidly progressive and severe, broad-spectrum antimicrobials are given urgently to patients with neutropenic fever as defined above. Vancomycin should only be given when there are clear indications for its use.


Candidates for empirical treatment with oral antimicrobials include those who are febrile but who have no evidence of focal infection or signs or symptoms of severe disease, like hypotension. Outpatient antimicrobials for neutropenic fever must be ordered only in consultation with Hematology-Oncology or
Infectious Diseases.
